title: Zion Foster Rejects Abandonment Claims After Twin Daughters' SMA Diagnosis in Jesy Nelson Documentary
text:
Zion Foster, ex-fiancé of singer Jesy Nelson, addresses backlash over his 'out of my depth' comments following the SMA type 1 diagnosis of their 14-month-old twin daughters, as documented in the Amazon Prime series 'Jesy Nelson: Life Changing.' He clarifies that his words reflected the shock of a complex medical reality, not a withdrawal from fatherhood, and reaffirms his commitment to his children while acknowledging the couple's split was precipitated by the traumatic diagnosis.
Zion Foster , the former fiancé of singer Jesy Nelson , has responded to public criticism that he abandoned his twin daughters following their diagnosis with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) type 1.
The twins, Story and Ocean, who are 14 months old, were diagnosed with the severe genetic disorder in January 2026. Their diagnosis and the family's emotional journey are featured in the Amazon Prime documentary series "Jesy Nelson: Life Changing," released on Friday. In the series, Zion is shown grappling with the devastating news, stating, "I'm not equipped to deal with this. I'm out of my depth; emotionally, physically and mentally.
At the moment I'm surviving. I just need to get help.
" Jesy, also featured, expressed empathy for his struggle, noting the immense pressure on a young father facing such a crisis. Their separation was announced later that same month. Jesy later explained in the documentary that she decided to end the relationship, saying, "I decided we would be better off apart," and acknowledging the immense challenge: "I think we're both thinking, 'how the f*** are we going to do this?
' And we will because we have to. We don't have a choice. It's really f****** hard.
" After some viewers interpreted his "out of my depth" comment as a sign of withdrawal, Zion used his Instagram Stories to clarify his position. He emphasized that his words were about confronting a complex medical reality, not about abandoning his children.
"When I said I was 'out of my depth', I wasn't saying I was walking away from my children or abandoning my responsibilities as a father," he wrote. "I was talking about the overwhelming reality of suddenly facing a rare and complex medical diagnosis that I knew nothing about. Being out of my depth meant I was learning. It meant I was trying to understand.
It never meant I didn't love my daughters or that I wasn't going to be there for them... Please don't mistake vulnerability for abandonment.
" He reaffirmed his love, calling his daughters "my world and always will be. " He also shared a video of himself working on a new song with the lyric "Out of my depth," suggesting a creative processing of the experience. Regarding the split, he stated, "Although I respect that, it does not change the fact that I remain committed to my daughters in every way I possibly can. This journey has been heartbreaking for all of us.
Nobody prepares you for news like this, and we're all navigating it in our own way.
" In the documentary, Jesy described the breakup as "inevitable" under the strain of the twins' illness. She explained, "It's a very traumatic thing that we've both been through. I think it's quite inevitable for things like this to happen to couples. I don't think it's a shock that we've broken up.
You'll either be a team or it'll tear you apart and unfortunately I feel that's what it's done to me and Zion.
" She insisted there is "no bad feeling" between them but that her "main priority" is her daughters. She added, "I just want to be the best mum with the best energy and positivity possible. The house was not like that when we were together. We're both dealing with this situation completely differently, and together we were clashing.
" Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a genetic disease that weakens muscles by damaging motor neurons in the spinal cord, leading to progressive muscle wasting. Type 1 SMA is the most severe form, appearing in infancy, and typically prevents children from sitting independently; without treatment, it historically led to early childhood mortality. Type 2 is intermediate severity, often preventing standing; Type 3 is milder, affecting the ability to rise from a seated position; and Type 4 has adult onset.
The diagnosis of SMA type 1 for infants is particularly challenging for families, requiring intensive care and emotional adjustment
